issues.detail: The Greek 'υπεταξεν' (hypetaxen) is an aorist active verb meaning 'subjugated' or 'placed under authority.' The Vietnamese 'chẳng từng khiến... phục dưới quyền' (never made... serve under the authority) adds a negation ('chẳng từng') and a continuous/perfective sense that is not present in the Greek text. The Greek is an affirmative statement of action, not a negation.
The Vietnamese translation changes the grammatical structure from 'subjugated the world' to 'didn't make the world serve,' which alters the directness of the action described in the Greek.
